comment: I really enjoyed taking Dr Walden's class!

A truly awesome professor. Is hilarious in class and has a good balance of work and fun in his class. 3 tests, chapter assignments on Connect each week. If you put in the work, there are no surprises and should be an easy good grade.
Uses a flipped classroom style. Do the readings and then come to class to clarify questions and get a full understanding. Weekly online homework, but they help with understanding the material.
If you complete the work on time and practice multiple choice questions like the ones on the quizzes, you should be fine and get a good grade.
He cares about his students and tries to make it easy to do well in the class.

Walden is a solid option if your goal is to get through the accounting requirement with the highest grade possible. I learned 90% of the material outside of class by reading the textbook and doing the homework and quizzes. I learned very little in class watching him skim over homework solutions and asking open ended questions.

Walden is a very nice and charismatic guy. He really wants all his students to do well and claims 50% of his students get an A in his course. While he isn't the best lecturer I learned all the material for on the online McGraw Hill textbook and found the class to be very doable. Not the best professor but the class is an easy A.

Dr. Walden is an incredibly caring professor who clearly wants the best for his students. Grading is mainly two mid-term exams and online quizzes throughout the year, and he also offers a low exam adjustment which helps students who improve over the semester.

This class is definitely challenging, but if you put in the work and stay ahead of your assignments, you will be fine. Professor Walden makes it his mission to support you and help you succeed in any way.

I really enjoyed this class with Professor Walden and it's clear that he wants all of his students to succeed. just do the homework, study the quizzes, and use the materials he provides to prepare for exams (every exam was very similar to what he said it would be). overall a very good option for 205 and would recommend taking him

One online quiz a week to go along with 2 midterms and a final. Homework's are graded as well so this can help boost your grade. Just participate in class and you will do fine. Great professor that always has a ton of energy and I would take him again.

Professor Walden inspires me. do the homework before class. you get graded by a lot but it keeps you in shape but you get grade dispersion. quizzes, online hw, smartbook, two midterms, etc. his lectures were good for you to do homework and practice in class bc his lectures are mostly review. very polite professor!

I had Dr. Walden for Financial ACCT 201 and Managerial ACCT 205 and did really well in both classes!  The class includes lectures and going over homework problems, of which he posts online after, which is incredibly helpful for reviewing for quizzes and exams.  Great professor, person, and wants his students to succeed.  Would highly recommend!

Dr. Walden is caring and tells very funny stories. I didn't learn too much from his lectures, but having the answers to the class problems, HW problems, and quizzes available for review made being prepared for quizzes and tests very straightforward. The content is relatively easy to understand.

He is incredibly supportive and readily available to help students. All assignments are conveniently online with reasonable deadlines, allowing for flexibility in managing workload. He also provides detailed feedback and I would highly recommend taking him!
Good professor with a good sense of humor and funny stories. Fairly lecture and practice problem heavy in class but overall a decently interesting course.

Dr Walden is a great guy. If you complete the HW assignments and understand the quizzes, the tests should be no problem. He is a very considerate grader, and the majority of students "Make an A." The lectures are not the most interesting (it's accounting), but he's hilarious so it makes up for it. In essence, you should take his class if you can.

Prof Walden is one of my favorite professors at UR. In class, expectations are clear on how to make an A. Assessments reflect the material laid out in class, textbook, and HW, which is manageable with no intention of waiting your time. Walden makes class lighthearted, treats all students with respect, and takes a personal interest in your learning.

The funniest teacher that there is to take. Gave me the benefit of the doubt with my final grade and truly cares about his students. If you have the chance to take him I recommend it due to how great of a guy Walden is.

Dr. Walden is clearly passionate about his students; however, his 205 course is definitely a "teach it yourself" class. Auto-graded quizzes, auto-graded homework, auto-graded tests. There is no partial credit given on tests because of m/c format. The stories about his tesla, son-in-laws, and wife kept class interesting though.

Dr.Walden is an inspiring, intelligent and supportive professor. Heis my fav professor at UR. I took both acct 201 and 205 with him. I hope i can take more classes with him. Extra credits are always given in midterm exams and finial. Reaching out to him before the exams is super helpful. Definitely take him .

Professor Walden was a great professor especially for non-accounting majors. The class was very straightforward and it is very possible to "make an A" as long as you do the work assigned. The homework can feel extensive at times, but you get an entire week to do it and he doesn't try to trick you on the tests. Definitely take him for ACCT 205!

Professor Walden is one of my favorite professors in the b-school. As non-accounting major, I feel Walden did a great job at making the class manageable. He was always free to meet anytime - he greatly cares about the success of his students. Expectations are clear and he is very accommodating for DAN students. Would recommend!
Dr. Walden is a wonderful professor. He treats students nice and offers clear and helpful materials. Exam questions are not hard and you will definitely earn A if you put efforts on the course.

Had him for 205 and 201: he is a great teacher. 201 was much easier, but 205 was still reasonable. His grading is fair, he is always open to meet, and he wants all of his students to "make an A." Though accounting is definitely a dull subject, his witty and genuine style of teaching makes class enjoyable. If a Walden is section open, take it!

I took Dr. Walden for both financial and managerial accounting. He's a funny guy and clearly cares about the content he teaches. His financial accounting class was definitely easier than the managerial class, but the managerial class was reasonable and the majority of the class ended up with a good grade.
Dr Walden is an amazing professor and easily my favorite at Richmond so far. If you have the opportunity to take his class do not hesitate to do so.

Second time taking Dr. Walden, as always a pleasure. His class sets the standard that if you want to earn an A, you can earn it so long as you put the work in. It isn't left to chance or luck, your grade is a direct reflection of the work you put in.

Professor Walden is one of the most caring professors and wants all of his students to excel in his course. He allowed us to drop our lowest quiz grade and I felt he was a very fair grader. In class he encourages his students to ask questions and is always happy to provide extra materials.

What a guy. I took him for 201 as well. It's not an online course, but it may as well be. Teach yourself from the textbook, auto graded homework, and auto graded quizzes. But his stories about his Tesla had me coming back for more.

Professor Walden is one of the nicest professors at this school and really wants every student to get an A. That being said, he is not a good lecturer and you will often have to teach yourself the material to do well.
HE IS NOT LECTURING AR ALL!!! He's reachable outside his class, but he's an awful lecturer, and never explains things clearly. DO NOT TAKE HIM

Dr. Walden is a great professor who wants his students to succeed and offers many learning opportunities to ensure this is possible. He is willing to meet with students for extra help and class is engaging as he encourages participation and is a charismatic lecturer. If you do the homework and make an effort this class is very manageable.

Awesome teacher! The material can be very dense at times and he provides so many opportunities to get help. The structure of the class is effective but a lot of time is still needed outside of the classroom. Read the textbook and do the practice problems and practice quizzes. Would definitely take him again!
Great teacher. Not the easiest class but if you put in the work you will succeed.

If you want a professor that really cares about you and your grade, this is the professor to take. Professor Walden makes accounting fun and is able to present information in a effective-entertaining way. His great charisma in the classroom, makes even the most boring moments exciting, overall great guy and profesor, highly recommend.

Dr. Walden was the best accounting professor. His classes were so funny and entertaining and he gives his students MANY chances to try and raise their grades. He was definitely one of my favorite professors since he actually cares about all his students. If you can, take his class!!
Gives a lot of extra credit and curves most exams.

Dr. Walden's grading is very straightforward, revolving around weekly quizzes and three tests. Practice problems are posted with answer keys allowing students to do well on assessments if they are willing to put in the effort. Tests and quizzes are curved and there are several extra credit opportunities. Kind and extremely funny.

Pretty straightforward class. As long as you pay attention and study for the tests, an A is easily attainable. He posts a lot of resources online, which are very useful for studying for the midterms and final.

Dr.Walden is a great professor! I liked his class and all assignments/quizzes were really straightforward. As long as you read the textbook thoroughly and do the hw questions everything will go well. He is nice and really does want you to succeed in his class. I took him this year and will be taking him again next year! :)

If you want to major in business, Dr. Walden's 201 is one of the best options! His class is very organized, with extra credit opportunities to help you boost your grades and many bonus points in exams. All class materials are uploaded on Blackboard timely so you can access them anytime. About 50% of students end up with A+/A/A-.

To be honest, this is my favorite professor at UR. He made me go from being afraid of accounting to being very interested in it now. He is humorous and prepares well for every class. And he is supportive, even at weekends he is willing to schedule online meetings to help students with their studies. I highly recommend his class!

While accounting can be a tough subject for many people professor Walden gives every student a genuine chance to get an A. The class can also get super boring at times but he makes jokes during the class all the time which make it more interesting
Great Professor. Very helpful and gives a lot of extra credit. If you put in the time you will do well.

Walden is the man. His lectures are about accounting, a difficult subject to make interesting, but his jokes and good spirit make class more than bearable. The hardest part of his class are the weekly quizzes (worth small % of grade), but his exams (worth >50% of grade) are not too hard and heavily curved, especially compared with his colleagues.

Walden gives you a solid foundation in accounting. Overwhelming at first between the readings, homework, practices quizzes, flashcards, etc, but in the end don't waste your time. Pay attention in class, ask questions, and go to him if needed. He wants you to succeed.

Walden's class was not hard. However, as someone most likely majoring in accounting this class was not very useful. Compared to other classes, this class is definitely easier, but you will not learn as much. Walden goes over the textbook that Hoyle wrote and uses notes from other teachers. He does not teach that well but he's knowledgeable & funny.

Dedicate a lot of time to this class, you won't be able to get the most out of this class. Go over his practice quizzes, make notes for yourself and try to get tutoring or go to his office hours. He gives a lot of chances for extra credit, and his quizzes are open book/note; sadly you cannot go back during the quizzes. He does not lecture in class.

Walden is a really nice guy and will do everything to help you "make an A". His lectures can be boring and his explanations aren't always the best. I thought accounting in general was easy, but I could see if you're struggling he would feel difficult. If you put a good effort, easy A for sure.
Walden is a very confusing teacher and does not do a good job of explaining accounting at all. Gives a lot of extra credit which makes up for it though.

Professor Walden is a very good teacher. Not only is he a very funny and nice guy, but he will always make sure you understand the material if you set aside the time to meet with him. Highly recommend to someone who wants to learn the basics of accounting.

I had Dr. Walden for Financial ACCT 201 and Managerial ACCT 205 and did really well in both classes!  The class includes lectures and going over homework problems, of which he posts online after, which is incredibly helpful for reviewing for quizzes and exams.  Great professor, person, and wants his students to succeed.  Would highly recommend!

Professor Walden was my favorite professor ever. His class is so easy as long as you do the work and dedicate some time to his class. All of his exams have extra credit problems and all the weekly quizzes are out of 110% so it's easy to end the class with an over 100% grade. He's one of the funniest professors and wants you to "Make an A".

This man is a horrible teacher. Simply does not know how to teach he just reads Powerpoint slides and says "in essence". Deducts points if you skip class. Some people can naturally understand accounting very easily and can do well in the class but if it doesn't come naturally for you and he is your professor: good luck my friend.

This man has been teaching at Richmond for 20 years and I'm pretty sure he only knows how to present powerpoints and freak out at students. You're better off buying "Managerial Accounting for Dummies" than wasting your time in this class. I'm still not even positive that his class wasn't just a semester long candid camera show.

He is by far the worst professor in the B school. Not only is he a bad teacher, he is also a terrible person. He tries to thinly veil his jaded personality and ineptitude with inspirational quotes and false claims of caring for his students. Also, if you take him, prepare to  hear the phrase "in essence" in the double digits.

He always compares himself to Hoyle but he's the exact opposite. Gives the amazing Accounting department at UR a terrible name. All you do is teach yourself because he won't stop handing out papers in class, putting the answers on the board, and expecting you to understand them while you scramble to write everything down.

This is one of the worst professors I've had at UR. Makes horrible, irrelevant jokes and does not teach the content in a clear, directional manner. Tends to ramble on about topics irrelevant to the course. Class consists of him giving out handouts and doing them in class while he waits for you to finish. Complete waste of time but a required class.

His email said that he always believes in students, but its not true at all. There is no requirement about attendance, but he remembers every time if you did not come to class, and he will score you on that. He said we can't argue scores with him, in other words, if he doesn't like you, he can give you an unarguable low score. DONT like him at all.
the worst professor I have ever met

Definitely my least favorite teacher that I've had and others agree. Really picks on specific students until they despise him. It's fine if you are the one he likes.  Learned nothing in class, but the book is useful. Got the highest grade on all three tests including a hundred on the final and received a b+ from an inexplicable participation grade.
We all know why he still has is job and its not because he is a good teacher. Stay away. You don't learn anything and you have to teach yourself.

Fairly easy class. You're allowed one hand written sheet of notes per test. 40% of grade is online homework, and it's hard not to get an A on the homework. Final grade can replace lowest test grade. So there's lots of chances to do well. Walden is very helpful and concerned about students.

By far the worst teacher I've had a UR.  Walden is lazy and uninterested and could care less about being in the classroom.  You must be able to teach yourself.  If you cannot do that, STAY AWAY.  He is a disservice to the bschool, and to accounting majors.  Do not take him for anything, you will regret it.

Very funny but cannot teach-ended up teaching myself from the textbook. Took him for 2 semesters. Pushes online assignments way too much when they really are not helpful at all and people just find ways around doing them. He weighs the final more than the tests but claims they are equal. Both semesters I had a *.6 and *.5 and both rounded down!!

Class is kind of confusing but there are lots of varied assignemnts (quizzes, tests, podcasts, online videos, etc.) and lots of them are easy completion grades. Tests are harder than I expected so don't put them off. I ended up with a B because I focused too much on Hoyle's class. If you put a small amount of effort into this class you should be ab
Lectures are very confusing. Must do a LOT of work outside of class. Class is completely opposite of hoyle's class.
No Comments
Class was boring.  Easy to do well but you don't really learn that much.

Dr. Walden seemed to be pushing for a good evaluation the entire semester.  He was always cheerful...almost too cheerful but is nice to his students. His course is extremely straight forward.  You know exactly what will be on the exam. Homework is 20% of the grade and it's easy to get a 100%. All homework and assignments are online.

His lectures are confusing and his tests cover literally every single thing he goes over. You will have to know it all backwards and forwards. However, he wants his students to do well and will let you drop poor quiz/test grades in many instances. Difficult class to get through but in the end he makes it easy to get a decent grade.

Nice guy although not nice too some students that he perceives aren't very interested (or intelligent).  No classes, all online, which I liked, although it kind of brings into question of what he's really getting paid to do.  If you want to do well in the class you have to keep up with online lessons.  I got an A+.

He cares about his students, gives extra credit, and may not be the worst professor on the planet, but his lectures are pointless and the accounting department at UR has so many other great professors that you really shouldn't take him unless you absolutely have to.

Theres a lot of material to cover in Mangerial Accounting, but he lets you do it at a good pace. A lot to learn but he gets it across well. Take notes and make sure to do ALL the homework and you'll be fine. Known to give extra credit. 4 tests all year and some other hmwk assignemnts is everything.
What the rater below says is true

I don't know why the previous reviewer was talking about; perhaps he or she just didn't understand the class.  This professor is talented and devoted to the discipline.  Please: no more emotional comments.  This professor is worth your time.
??? Elmo and Cookie Monster???  Who moved my cheese???  You will be left dazed and confused by many of his lectures, wondering in what parallel universe any of it has anything to do with accounting.
No Comments
